issues.claim: The Great Wall of China is visible to the naked eye from the Moon, according to NASA.
issues.key_finding: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen unaided from the Moon.
issues.rationale: NASA explicitly says the Great Wall is not visible from the Moon, directly contradicting the claim about what NASA says. The European Space Agency likewise notes that even from the much closer International Space Station, seeing it requires a zoomed photograph rather than the naked eye.
issues.suggested_rewrite: The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, according to NASA.

issues.claim: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1899 and stands about 450 metres tall in central Paris.
issues.key_finding: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 and stands 330 metres tall.
issues.rationale: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, but the claim gets both its completion year and height substantially wrong. It was completed in 1889, not 1899, and stands about 330 metres tall, not 450 metres. The location is correct, but it does not rescue the claim’s two defining factual assertions.
issues.suggested_rewrite: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 and stands about 330 metres tall in central Paris.

verification.claim: The Great Wall of China is visible to the naked eye from the Moon, according to NASA.
verification.key_finding: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen unaided from the Moon.
verification.executive_summary: NASA explicitly says the Great Wall of China cannot be seen with the naked eye from the Moon, the opposite of the position attributed to it. Scientific American independently supports that conclusion. Photographs and reports about visibility from low Earth orbit do not establish visibility from the much greater lunar distance.
verification.suggested_rewrite: The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, according to NASA.
warnings: Visibility from low Earth orbit does not establish visibility from the Moon.
Photographs taken with cameras do not show what the naked eye can see.
The claim attributes to NASA a position that NASA explicitly rejects.

verification.key_finding: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 and stands 330 metres tall.
verification.executive_summary: The claim gives the wrong completion year and substantially overstates the Eiffel Tower’s height. It was completed in 1889 and stands 330 metres tall including its antenna, according to official tower records and structural references. Its location in central Paris is broadly accurate, but the two numerical assertions are not.
verification.suggested_rewrite: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 and stands about 330 metres tall in central Paris.
warnings: The 330-metre figure includes the antenna; measurements excluding it are lower.
Several official sources come from the same operator and should not be counted as independent confirmations.

claims.claim: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, according to Britannica.

positions.text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, as [Britannica explains](https://www.britannica.com/science/boiling-point).

assessment.rationale: Britannica explicitly states that water boils at 100 °C at sea level, with the usual qualification that boiling temperature varies with atmospheric pressure. This is consistent with the normal boiling point of pure water at standard sea-level pressure; the claim is accurate as worded, though “sea level” is a practical shorthand for that pressure.

claims.claim: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level.

positions.text: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level. Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level.

assessment.rationale: Mount Everest has the highest summit elevation of any mountain, at approximately 8,848.86 metres above sea level. Mauna Kea is taller if measured from its underwater base to its summit, but that does not contradict the claim’s explicit above-sea-level measure.
